newsitem.title: UK: Independent advisers want division in Super-SIB.
newsitem.headline: Independent advisers want division in Super-SIB.

text.p: Britain's independent financial advisers (IFAs) on Tuesday called for the proposed Securities and Investments Board (SIB), commonly known as Super-SIB, to include a separate division for them.

The IFA Association, whose members are currently regulated by the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) says smaller firms of advisers have been swamped by excessive paperwork and complex rules because they are bracketed with large insurance companies that have big direct sales forces.
"A new 'professional advisers' division of the new SIB would regulate with greater understanding of the needs and difficulties of smaller businesses," the Association said in a statement.
It added the current regulation had gone too far in stifling competition and growth with "overbearing rules and excessive and prescriptive regulation."

Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown proposed a new financial regulator in May, which would also include responsibility for banking, currently regulated by the Bank of England. The new authority would bring together the current regime, which consists of the SIB umbrella over three front-line self-regulatory organisations.
A task force representing the current regulators is currently working on a report for Brown which is expected to be handed over by the end of the month.
